subject: EdgeProof on-prem deployment: cluster topology constraints and storage tiers
messages:
From: Alicia Gomez <alicia@edgeproof.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@edgeproof.com
Date: Tue, 25 Jun 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: On-prem intake: single-rack constraints and storage tiers (attachment)

Hi Rishi,

Thanks for taking this on. We are evaluating Redwood for an on-prem/private deployment at our primary site. A few constraints up front:

- Single rack footprint (42U) with two top-of-rack switches and an isolated aggregation switch.
- No direct internet egress from the cluster except via a permitted proxy appliance (outbound TLS only).
- GPU capacity expected initially: 2 x A100-class nodes (burst to 4 for training windows).
- Node pools: control plane (3 VMs/supervisor nodes), compute-gpu, compute-cpu.
- Storage: hot NVMe for model ephemeral KV/cache, warm replicated blockstore for persistent weights and logs, archive to on-site object storage.
- Compliance: SOC 2 readiness, need KMS/HSM integration and audit logs surfaced to our SIEM.
- Timeline: aim to be production-ready in ~8 weeks.

Attached is our intake spreadsheet (edgeproof-reqs.xlsx) with rack inventory and network CIDR ranges. Can you confirm if Redwood supports:

1) Single-rack private cluster with the egress/proxy constraint?
2) A recommended storage mapping (which data on NVMe vs blockstore vs archive)?
3) Any blockers around KMS integration and audit log exports?

Appreciate any quick notes and if we can schedule a 60-minute design workshop next week.

Best,
Alicia Gomez
Head of Infrastructure, EdgeProof Systems
alicia@edgeproof.com
+1 415 555 0132

Subject: Re: On-prem intake: single-rack constraints and storage tiers (proposal attached)

Hi Alicia,

Thanks for the detailed intake and the spreadsheet — that's very helpful. Short answers up front: yes, we can support the single-rack private cluster with the egress/proxy constraint, and we have a pattern we recommend for the storage tiers. I've attached an initial topology sketch (rishi-edgeproof-topology-v1.png) and included clarifying notes below.

Recommended high-level topology (summary):
- Control plane: 3 management VMs on dedicated VLAN, each with disk encryption and a read-only audit export path to your SIEM collector.
- Worker pools:
  - gpu-worker-pool: 2 x GPU servers (NVMe local for ephemeral KV & model cache), tainted to ensure GPU scheduling. Burst plan supports scaling to 4 nodes behind capacity gating.
  - cpu-worker-pool: general compute for preprocessing and auxiliary services.
  - infra-worker-pool: small instances for logging, Prometheus, and CSI controller with anti-affinity rules.
- Storage mapping:
  - NVMe local (ephemeral): model KV cache, prefix cache, temporary sampling material.
  - Blockstore (network-attached, replicated across two JBOD shelves): persistent model weights, indexes, and checkpoint storage. Recommend encrypted LUKS on the block volumes with KMS-wrapped keys.
  - On-site object archive: daily lifecycle from blockstore snapshots; retain according to your RTO/RPO.
- Networking/egress: all egress routed through your proxy appliance IP with strict egress ACLs. We can support a forced-proxy NAT gateway inside the VPC and disable direct outbound via egress-route policies.
- KMS/HSM & audit: Redwood supports customer-managed KMS (via KMIP/HSM connectors) and will stream audit events to your SIEM (syslog or TLS endpoint). We will need a short key-wrap policy and a role for the HSM access.

Open clarifying questions:
1) Do you require local persistent volume encryption to be managed by your HSM only, or is using your KMS (cloud/HSM) acceptable?
2) What's the expected working set size for models in GPU memory vs warm storage (rough GB per model)? That drives NVMe capacity.
3) Are there any PCIe-level constraints (e.g., NVMe passthrough required) or do you want us to use software-managed caching?

Next steps:
- Schedule a 60-min design workshop (I'm available Thu 2029-06-27 or Mon 2029-07-01).
- We'll deliver a Scope-of-Work and a draft SOW/Statement-of-Technical-Requirements within 5 business days after the workshop.

I've included Marissa (solutions lead) and Neha (network/security) to help refine node sizing and network gating.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Director, Deployment Engineering | Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 26 Jun 2029 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: EdgeProof node sizing + autoscale notes

Internal - do not forward

Quick internal notes following Alicia's ask and Rishi's sketch:

- Node sizing:
  - GPU nodes: propose 2 x 80GB A100 nodes initially (8 GPUs across 2 hosts if they want multi-GPU pods) with local 4TB NVMe for cache. Reserve headroom for burst to 4 hosts; consider hot-swap licensing if they need ephemeral bursts.
  - CPU nodes: mix of 32-core high-memory instances for preprocessing pipelines; 3 nodes to start with HPA.
- Autoscaling/throughput gating:
  - We'll use Redwood's burst-capacity policy that gates burst requests via queue depth and token bucket to avoid saturating the single rack's network.
- Storage/IO considerations:
  - NVMe wear-leveling: suggest nightly cache trims and write amplification controls.
  - Blockstore replication: at least N+1 across two shelves to survive a single-shelf failure.
- Network constraints:
  - With forced proxy egress, we need an internal egress NAT and a health check path for control plane telemetry. Neha, will the SIEM accept TLS push on 443, or do they need a specific port?

I'll prep a short decision matrix for the workshop outlining trade-offs (cost vs latency vs durability).

-Marissa
Solutions Engineering, Redwood Inference
